SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #9
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Where does the sun rise? (1 mark)
   A. In the east
   B. In the north
   C. In the west
   D. In the south

2. What should you find first when you read a map? (1 mark)
   A. The names of rivers
   B. The colours
   C. The size of the paper
   D. The north arrow

3. A pupil faces the rising sun in the morning. Which direction is on the pupil's left hand? (1 mark)
   A. North
   B. East
   C. West
   D. South

4. A pupil faces the rising sun in the morning. Which direction is on the pupil's right hand? (1 mark)
   A. North
   B. East
   C. West
   D. South

5. Which valley runs from north to south through Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. The Coast Valley
   B. The Great Rift Valley
   C. The Kisumu Valley
   D. The Tana Valley

6. Where should you shelter during a thunderstorm? (1 mark)
   A. Under a tall tree
   B. In an open field
   C. Beside a river
   D. In a strong building

7. Why do farmers plan their work using seasons? (1 mark)
   A. Seasons tell the price of clothes
   B. Seasons decide school holidays only
   C. Crops need the right weather to grow and be harvested
   D. Seasons decide the colour of soil

8. What is a monument? (1 mark)
   A. A structure built to remember a person or event
   B. A market
   C. A river
   D. A bus

9. What is an artefact? (1 mark)
   A. A river
   B. A type of weather
   C. A mountain
   D. An object made and used by people in the past

10. What is barter? (1 mark)
   A. Stealing
   B. Buying with money only
   C. Giving things away
   D. Exchanging one thing for another without money

11. Which area is most likely to be sparsely populated? (1 mark)
   A. A busy town
   B. A lakeshore with fish
   C. A fertile highland
   D. A very dry area with little rain

12. Who usually passes traditional culture on to children? (1 mark)
   A. Only strangers
   B. Parents, grandparents and elders
   C. Only shops
   D. Machines

13. How can a school show traditional culture? (1 mark)
   A. By stopping all games
   B. By locking classrooms
   C. By closing the library
   D. By holding a culture day with songs and dances

14. What does respect mean? (1 mark)
   A. Treating people and things with honour
   B. Ignoring people
   C. Insulting people
   D. Breaking things

15. Which of these economic activities is a service? (1 mark)
   A. A crop of maize
   B. Teaching
   C. A stone
   D. A fish

16. Which activity earns money from visitors to game parks and beaches? (1 mark)
   A. Quarrying
   B. Fishing
   C. Mining
   D. Tourism

17. What raw material is used in a cement factory? (1 mark)
   A. Limestone
   B. Fish
   C. Sugarcane
   D. Milk

18. What is a raw material? (1 mark)
   A. A machine
   B. A worker
   C. A finished product
   D. A material used to make something new

19. Which of these is a benefit of industries? (1 mark)
   A. They provide jobs
   B. They stop trade
   C. They close schools
   D. They remove roads

20. How do industries help farmers? (1 mark)
   A. They buy the farmers' produce
   B. They stop rain
   C. They cut farms
   D. They teach only

21. Why is teamwork important in a project? (1 mark)
   A. It shares work and helps the project succeed
   B. It makes the project fail
   C. It stops others helping
   D. It makes work harder

22. You find a lost pencil that belongs to a classmate. What should you do? (1 mark)
   A. Hide it
   B. Keep it
   C. Sell it
   D. Return it to the owner

23. Who can be a role model? (1 mark)
   A. A teacher or an elder
   B. Nobody
   C. Only a president
   D. Only a rich person

24. Which is a good way to develop a quality like punctuality? (1 mark)
   A. Wait for others to do it
   B. Practise it once a year
   C. Ignore it
   D. Practise it every day

25. Which activity builds peace in school? (1 mark)
   A. A fight
   B. A peace poster competition
   C. Spreading rumours
   D. Cheating

26. What is discrimination? (1 mark)
   A. Sharing
   B. Helping
   C. Treating some people unfairly because of who they are
   D. Treating everyone equally

27. What is campaigning? (1 mark)
   A. Counting votes
   B. Telling voters why they should choose you
   C. Announcing results
   D. Throwing away ballots

28. Why is a Children's Government important? (1 mark)
   A. It punishes children
   B. It closes the school
   C. It stops learning
   D. It gives pupils a voice and shares responsibility

29. Which item usually comes first on an agenda? (1 mark)
   A. Reports
   B. Opening prayer or song
   C. Suggestions
   D. Closing remarks

30. Which item usually comes last on an agenda? (1 mark)
   A. Opening prayer
   B. Reading of minutes
   C. Closing remarks
   D. Reports

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. List four factors a company thinks about before building a factory. (4 marks)

32. State three roles of an MCA. (3 marks)

33. Explain what a raw material is and give one example. (2 marks)

34. Explain why a monument is built. (2 marks)

35. Give two reasons why some areas are sparsely populated. (2 marks)

36. Explain how you can find east in the morning without a compass. (2 marks)

37. Draw a compass rose and label the four cardinal points. (3 marks)

38. Describe how to stay safe during a visit to a factory. Give four rules. (4 marks)

39. Write a peace message and explain how it can help other pupils. (4 marks)

40. Give two traditional foods and say where each is popular. (4 marks)

41. A group spent Ksh 900 and earned Ksh 600. Say whether this is a profit or a loss and find the amount. Suggest two reasons why it may have happened. (4 marks)

42. Explain how a cultural centre is different from a museum. (3 marks)

43. Describe how you would draw a sketch map of your county in five steps. (5 marks)

44. Give three factors that promote peace in school. (3 marks)

45. Draw a side view of the land showing a mountain, a valley and a plain and label them. (5 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #9 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — In the east
   The sun rises in the east and sets in the west.

2. D — The north arrow
   Finding north first helps you read all other directions.

3. A — North
   Facing east, north is on the left and south is on the right.

4. D — South
   Facing east, south is on the right hand.

5. B — The Great Rift Valley
   The Great Rift Valley runs through Kenya.

6. D — In a strong building
   Lightning can strike tall trees, so a building is safer.

7. C — Crops need the right weather to grow and be harvested
   Planting and harvesting depend on rain and dry weather.

8. A — A structure built to remember a person or event
   Monuments remind people of important people or events.

9. D — An object made and used by people in the past
   Artefacts include tools, pots and clothes.

10. D — Exchanging one thing for another without money
   Barter means swapping goods, such as a goat for grain.

11. D — A very dry area with little rain
   Dry areas make farming and water supply hard.

12. B — Parents, grandparents and elders
   Culture is taught in families and communities.

13. D — By holding a culture day with songs and dances
   A culture day lets pupils share their heritage.

14. A — Treating people and things with honour
   Respect is showing care and honour.

15. B — Teaching
   Teaching is work done to help others.

16. D — Tourism
   Tourism serves visitors.

17. A — Limestone
   Cement is made using limestone.

18. D — A material used to make something new
   Raw materials are used to make products.

19. A — They provide jobs
   Industries employ people.

20. A — They buy the farmers' produce
   Factories need farm produce as raw materials.

21. A — It shares work and helps the project succeed
   Sharing roles makes work easier.

22. D — Return it to the owner
   Returning shows honesty.

23. A — A teacher or an elder
   Ordinary people can be good role models.

24. D — Practise it every day
   Habits grow with practice.

25. B — A peace poster competition
   Competitions on peace teach and encourage it.

26. C — Treating some people unfairly because of who they are
   Discrimination is unfair treatment.

27. B — Telling voters why they should choose you
   Candidates campaign before elections.

28. D — It gives pupils a voice and shares responsibility
   It teaches leadership and democracy.

29. B — Opening prayer or song
   Meetings begin with an opening.

30. C — Closing remarks
   Meetings end with closing remarks.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: Raw materials, market, transport, and water and power. Accept workers or land.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each factor.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Represent the ward, make county laws, and approve the budget. Accept checking the governor.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each role.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: A raw material is a material used to make something new, for example sugarcane used to make sugar.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for example.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: A monument is built to remind people of an important person or event so that they remember it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for reminding people, 1 mark for the idea of a person or event.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: Very little rain and no water, and thick forests, swamps or steep land. Accept game parks or few roads.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: Face the direction where the sun rises. That direction is east.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for using the rising sun, 1 mark for naming east.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: A drawing with N at the top, E on the right, S at the bottom and W on the left.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for neat drawing, 1 mark for N at top, 1 mark for E, S and W correct.

38. (4 marks)
   Answer: Stay with the group, do not touch machines, listen to the guide, and wear safety clothing if given.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: Talk, do not fight. It reminds pupils to solve problems with words, so there are fewer fights and everyone feels safe.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a clear message, 1 mark for correct language, 2 marks for the explanation.

40. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: githeri in central Kenya and fish with ugali near Lake Victoria. Accept other correct examples.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each food and 1 mark for each correct place.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: It is a loss of Ksh 300. Sales may have been low because the price was too high or not enough people knew about the goods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for loss, 1 mark for the amount 900 - 600 = 300, 1 mark for each reason.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: A museum mainly keeps and shows objects. A cultural centre lets people see and join in living culture such as dances and crafts. Some places do both.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each description and 1 mark for the difference.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: Draw the county outline. Draw the sub-county boundaries. Write the names of the sub-counties. Show the neighbouring counties around the edge. Add a north arrow, a title and a key, then colour it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Respect, sharing and forgiveness. Accept honesty, listening or fairness.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each factor.

45. (5 marks)
   Answer: A drawing with a high peak labelled mountain, a low dip labelled valley and a flat area labelled plain.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct shape drawn and 1 mark for each label, up to 5 marks.
